resources.string: Drag the images to match with the correct handsign.
Are you sure you want to logout?
Make a fist. Keep your thumb on the side of your fist, pointing to the side, not across the front of your other fingers.
Keep your fingers straight and together, palm facing forward. Tuck your thumb across your palm.
Curve your hand into a “C” shape, with your fingers and thumb forming a half circle.
Touch your thumb and middle, ring, and pinky fingertips together while raising your index finger straight up.
Curl your fingers toward your palm and place your thumb across them, forming a small curved shape like the lowercase \'e\'.
Form an “OK” sign — connect your thumb and index finger to make a circle while the other three fingers are raised.
Hold your hand sideways with your thumb and index finger pointing outward, as if showing a small distance between them.
Hold out your index and middle finger together, pointing to the side, while the rest are closed — like a sideways peace sign.
Raise your pinky finger while keeping the rest closed in a fist.
Start with the “I” sign, then draw a “J” in the air using your pinky finger.
Raise your index and middle fingers apart (like a “V”), then place your thumb between them.
Extend your index finger upward and your thumb sideways to form an “L” shape.
Place your thumb under your first three fingers (index, middle, ring), with your pinky out or folded — representing the three bumps of “M”.
Similar to “M” but only place your thumb under two fingers (index and middle) — forming the two bumps of “N”.
Start with the “N” sign, then make a small waving motion (side to side).
Start with the “N” sign, then make a “G” sign.
Form a full “O” with your fingers and thumb touching each other to make a round circle.
Make a “K” shape, then tilt your wrist downward — the index finger points forward.
Form the same shape as “G”, but point it slightly downward.
Cross your index and middle fingers.
Similar to “A” sign, but make a fist with your thumb crossing in front of your fingers.
Make a “thumbs up” gesture, and place your index finger on top of your thumb.
Raise your index and middle fingers together, touching side by side.
Raise your index and middle fingers apart to form a “V” sign.
Raise your index, middle, and ring fingers to form a “W”.
Bend your index finger to form a hook while keeping the rest closed.
Extend your thumb and pinky finger out, keeping the other fingers closed.
Use your index finger to draw a “Z” shape in the air.
Raise your dominant hand near your temple, like giving a casual salute. Move your hand outward slightly as if greeting someone from a distance.

Place both hands together in front of your chest, palms facing downward. Then, rotate your hands outward so the palms face up, as if showing or presenting something. And point your index finger forward.
Form a fist with your dominant hand and place it over your chest. Move your fist in a small circular motion a few times.
Place both hands near your lips with fingertips touching the mouth.
Touch your lips lightly with the fingertips of one hand, then move your hand forward.
Raise your index finger while keeping the other fingers closed into your palm. Make sure your palm faces outward. This simple handshape clearly represents the number one.
Extend your index and middle fingers together while keeping the other fingers folded down. Your palm should face outward, similar to a peace sign, representing the number two.
Raise your thumb, index finger, and middle finger while keeping your ring and pinky fingers folded down. Hold your palm facing outward — this represents the number three.
Extend all four fingers upward — index, middle, ring, and pinky — with your thumb tucked against your palm. This clearly represents the number four.
Spread out all five fingers with your palm facing forward, as if showing your whole hand. This open-hand gesture symbolizes the number five.

Touch the tip of your thumb to the tip of your pinky finger, forming a small circle. Keep your other three fingers extended upward. This gesture visually connects the smallest and largest fingers to represent the number six.
Touch the tip of your thumb to the tip of your ring finger while keeping the other fingers extended. This creates a shape that symbolizes the number seven.
Touch the tip of your thumb to your middle finger, with your other fingers extended upward. This shape is used to represent the number eight.
Touch the tip of your thumb to your index finger to form a small circle, keeping the rest of your fingers extended. It’s similar to an \'OK\' sign — symbolizing the number nine.
Make a closed fist and slightly shake it side to side, or extend your thumb upward like a thumbs-up sign. This gesture is used to represent the number ten.
Hold one hand open in front of your chest with your palm facing upward. Move your hand slightly side to side while raising your eyebrows.
Raise your index finger of one hand and use the index finger of your other hand to trace a small circular motion around it. Then, point your finger forward while slightly raising your eyebrows.
Raise both of your hands and move it side to side gently, with your palm facing outward. Tilt your head slightly and raise your eyebrows to show you’re asking a question.
Hold both hands in front of your chest with thumbs extended upward and other fingers closed. Move each hand alternately up and down, as if comparing two choices.

Form a slightly open hand near your chin. Gently close it up until you form a shape that looks like you are grabbing something tiny with all of your fingers. Use a curious facial expression to show you’re asking, \'Who?\'
Touch your forehead with your fingertips, then move your hand outward and downward while changing it into a \'Y\' sign (thumb and pinky extended).
Place both hands together in front of your chest, palms facing downward. Then, rotate your hands outward so the palms face up, as if showing or presenting something.
Form the letter \'M\' by placing your thumb under your first three fingers. Then make a small circular motion in front of your chest.
Make the letter \'T\' by placing your index finger on top of your thumb. Move your hand in a small circle in front of your chest.
Form the letter \'W\' using your three middle fingers raised, with your thumb and pinky down. Move your hand slightly in a circular motion in front of your chest.

Combine the letters \'T\' and \'H\' in sequence. First, form the letter \'T\' with your index finger on top of your thumb, then slide your hand into the \'H\' shape (index and middle fingers extended together, palm facing sideways).
Make the letter \'F\' by touching your index finger and thumb together to form a small circle, while the other fingers stay extended. Move the hand slightly in front of your chest.
Form the letter \'S\' by making a closed fist with your thumb placed over your fingers. Move your hand in a small circular motion in front of your chest.
Hold both open hands with palms facing forward. Then move them slightly in a circular motion together.
You have successfully completed all available lessons and quizzes in Senyas. You\'ve taken a huge step in learning Filipino Sign Language. We\'re proud of you!
